verdict: JPMorgan closed 2024 with net income up 50% to $14.0B, as trading and investment-banking fees surged — reported revenue rose 11% to $42.8B even though net interest income slipped 3%.
costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.4B of loans were charged off in the quarter and reserves were built by about $0.3B on a net basis.

kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

kpis.label: Credit costs
kpis.note: $2.4B charged off, plus a small net reserve build

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, down 3% as lower rates and deposit-margin compression outweighed balance growth.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 34% as Markets revenue rose 21% to $7.0B and investment banking fees jumped 48%.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,309M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($2,126M).

footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $43.7B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $42.8B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $42.8B reported (GAAP), used here, or $43.7B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way. The rows reconcile to the $100 total within a cent of rounding.

takeaways.title: Markets and deal fees powered the quarter
takeaways.text: Markets revenue rose 21% to $7.0B — equities up 22%, fixed income up 20% — and investment banking fees jumped 48%, more than covering the 3% dip in net interest income.

takeaways.title: Elite profitability to close the year
takeaways.text: Return on tangible common equity was 21%, and the bank kept $14.0B — about 33 cents of every reported revenue dollar — capping a record $58.5B of profit for 2024 as a whole.

takeaways.title: Credit costs stayed contained
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses was $2.6B — $2.4B of loans charged off, mostly in cards, plus a small net reserve build — down from $2.8B a year ago even as card balances grew.
